items.title: Elizabeth O'Kelly Kerrigan Interview, 1958-05-04
items.q: South Stan was not the leader, but he was a member of the band. And that, they played for private parties.

ctx.x: Well, uh, can you tell me how long it lasted, what, you know, when people stopped listening to it, and then when they started again, they established it?

Well, I think that there were a lot of, uh, these sweet bands that got popular. But, uh, was Puron playing when you, uh, made your debut? But he died, uh, not too long after that. And, uh, then this, let's say, five or six years, or maybe a little bit longer than that, the people started going in for the, you know, the, uh, sweet type of music. Or during the 30s, they, they liked that type. And, uh, I think Puron, I mean, uh, um, South Stan got his dog back here at the pass. Because, you know, John Curran got him…
Well, that's fine. Thank you, ma'am.
